purpose: Visual module integration on screenshots of the actual game robot; not a Godot model integration

specs.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit and compositing.
Asset type: garage module placement mockup on the ACTUAL game robot.
Image 1 is the EDIT TARGET: a newly captured screenshot from the actual Godot game. Image 2 is an ACCESSORY DESIGN REFERENCE only, not a replacement robot or replacement scene.
Edit Image 1 very conservatively: preserve the exact recognizable original robot, its cyclops ivory head, cyan eye, small head-mounted optics, scarf, torn red cloth, red flag, rolled bedroll backpack, chest armor and cyan circular heart, exposed joints, original legs, feet, stance, proportions, textures, camera, lighting, workshop walls and round service platform. Preserve the original screenshot's moderately rough game-rendered surface finish and lighting. Do not beautify, reinvent, remesh, recolor or replace the robot. No new character. Do not replace the background. Keep the entire original robot visible and original portrait crop.
Add only ONE accessory inspired by Image 2, physically attached to this exact robot with a sensible compact bracket or collar, correct perspective, contact shadow, occlusion and matching worn ivory/ochre material. Reduce the reference accessory to believable arm/armor size: a small distinctive functional shape, not an enormous object strapped to the robot. The original head and glowing chest heart must be completely unobstructed. The added part must remain recognizable at whole-robot scale. No floating module, no detached accessory alongside the robot, no separate pedestal, no inset product image, no repeated rectangular casings, no extra accessories from other modules.
No interface or invented game text. Add only a small unobtrusive French module name in clear ivory type in the upper-left background margin, without covering any robot pixels.
ONE added accessory: TRAQUEUR. Shrink the spherical cyan mechanical eye and ochre eyelid from Image 2 and attach it on a SHORT swiveling bracket on the OUTBOARD side of the robot's LEFT shoulder, the shoulder nearest the viewer on the RIGHT side of Image 1. Preserve the original shoulder plate beneath it. The module is a small shoulder-mounted watchful eye looking forwards, diameter about 50 percent of the original robot's head width, total eye-and-bracket height no more than the original head height. The bracket is flush bolted to the shoulder armor, not a freestanding platform. It does not sit on top of the head and does not replace the robot's original eye or head optics. Keep it away from the scarf, chest heart, flag and bedroll. Match the source robot's rough worn game texture rather than rendering a hyper-realistic glossy object.
Text (verbatim): "TRAQUEUR".
